# Implement block: Scatter Collage Hero (SwiftUI)

You are adding the "Scatter Collage Hero" block from Native Cook to the user's iOS app. The block already exists as working SwiftUI code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

An airy collage for a meditation library: two dozen photos of different sizes float on an off-white page with lots of space between them, small and faint near the middle and larger towards the edges, as if the whole field were drifting slowly towards you and up past the top. A serif wordmark, "Stillhour", and a line under it sit top left beside a round avatar, and a row of chips (All, Meditation, Yoga, Breath, Sleep) along the bottom dims the photos outside the chosen one. Tapping a photo flies it out of the collage into a full-screen hero: the photo fills the screen, its guide's name, a two-line serif title such as "Salt / Balance" with the second line in italic and a line about it rise in, with the time and date either side of a pale green Start pill and a strip of four thumbnails along the bottom. Swiping sideways pushes in the next hero, and dragging down or tapping the chevron puts the photo back in its place in the collage.

**Motion.** The collage is drawn on a single canvas. Each of the 24 tiles lives on a cycle: it is born near a vanishing point at 50% across and 52% down, a golden angle (2.4 rad) round from the last one, and grows five times over its cycle, exponentially so the zoom feels even, moving out to 92% of the width and 60% of the height times a per-tile reach of 0.84 to 1.16; its longer side ends at 236 pt on a 402 pt screen (times 0.82 to 1.18). A tile stays hidden for the first 14% of its cycle, fades in until 36% and fades out over the last 14%, and its corners are 3 pt plus 5% of its shorter side. Far tiles are drawn first. Tapping a tile flies it to the full screen on a spring (duration 700 ms, damping ratio 0.86) with a light haptic, its corners closing to 0, while the other tiles fade out; the hero's copy rises 22 pt into place line by line from 66% of the way, each line 4% later and taking 14%. The heroes are the tiles fully on screen, up to eight, read top to bottom. Swiping sideways pages between them, one screen per hero, the photo lagging its frame by 42% of the distance and the copy by 30%, so the next hero pushes the last one out in layers; past the first or last the pager gives way at 28%; on release the page is thrown 0.22 s ahead (never more than one hero) and a spring (520 ms, 0.88) carries it there, with a selection haptic. The thumbnails lift 5 pt and gain a white ring as their hero comes to the front, and the strip slides to keep the active one second. Dragging down shrinks the hero by up to 30% over 55% of the screen, following the finger, rounding its corners to 44 pt and letting the collage back in up to 70% over the first 30% of the screen; a release past 120 pt or faster than 750 pt/s closes it into its tile's current place on a spring (640 ms, 0.9) carrying the finger's speed, anything else springs back (420 ms, 0.82). The chips dim the photos outside the chosen category to 16% over 360 ms on an ease-in-out curve (0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) while the green pill slides to it on a spring (420 ms, 0.8). Each photo fades in over 0.4 s once loaded (480 px wide for the collage, 1000 px for the heroes, which fade over the small copy in 0.3 s). The self-playing demo loops every 15 s: the field flies, slows to a stop over 0.6 s as a tile near the middle opens at 3.2 s, pages to the next hero at 6.3 s, is dragged down 150 pt at 8.6 s and closes at 9 s, and the field starts flying again over 0.85 s at 9.15 s; every tile makes exactly one cycle per loop, so the loop has no seam. A touch stops the demo for 3.5 s, 7 s while a hero is open, after which an open hero closes and the loop starts over. Under reduced motion the field holds still, the demo does not play and the hero cross-fades in and out over 240 ms without flying.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [ScatterCollageHeroDemo.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Blocks/Media/ScatterCollageHero/ScatterCollageHeroDemo.swift)

### Files of the block

- [ScatterCollageHero.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Blocks/Media/ScatterCollageHero/ScatterCollageHero.swift)
- [ScatterCollageHeroEngine.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Blocks/Media/ScatterCollageHero/ScatterCollageHeroEngine.swift)
- [ScatterCollageHeroMotion.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Blocks/Media/ScatterCollageHero/ScatterCollageHeroMotion.swift)
- [ScatterCollageHeroSessions.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Blocks/Media/ScatterCollageHero/ScatterCollageHeroSessions.swift)

### Shared helpers the block uses

- [swift/NativeCook/Shared/ComponentSupport.swift](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/swift/NativeCook/Shared/ComponentSupport.swift)

### Frameworks

It needs no framework beyond SwiftUI.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced iOS engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference in the iOS Simulator or on a device. A SwiftUI preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and curves. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an iOS app built with Xcode (an `.xcodeproj`, an `.xcworkspace` or a Swift package with an app target). If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app target, its deployment target and its Swift version.
- SwiftUI, UIKit or both, and how a screen is shown today: `NavigationStack`, a coordinator, a tab bar, a storyboard.
- How files join the target: a folder the project synchronises, or a file list in the project that you have to extend.
- Conventions: folder layout, naming, where colours, fonts and assets live.
- Type names the app already uses, so the block's types do not collide with them.

### 3. Read the block

- Swift files in a module do not import each other, so the demo alone will not lead you to the rest. The list above names every file of the block: read them all.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's initialiser and its defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- The source app targets iOS 17. If the host targets an older system, check each API the block uses and tell the user what would have to change before you lower anything. Do not raise the host's deployment target without asking.
- If a type or function name of the block already exists in the app, rename the block's one, in every file that uses it, and say that you did.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block uses next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.
- In a UIKit app, show the block through a `UIHostingController`.

### 5. Bring it in

- Add the block's files to the app target, keeping their names.
- Copy its asset catalogs, loose resources and fonts, and check that the names the code asks for match the names in the bundle: a wrong name compiles and then shows nothing.
- A `.metal` file has to be compiled into the same target as the code that calls its function.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build the app target for a simulator with `xcodebuild` or the project's own script, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Run it and use the block: every state, every gesture, light and dark appearance if the block follows them, and once with Reduce Motion on.
- If the build or the simulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
